rewrites.//: UNA sola llamada para el movil: la base de parkings ya fusionada [PARKINGS-ONE-CALL-MERGED-001]. ⛔ El `.json` del path NO es cosmetico y no se quita: la regla de cabeceras `**/!(*.*)` de abajo casa CUALQUIER ruta cuyo ultimo segmento no tenga punto, asi que con `/api/parkings` el Hosting pisaba el `Cache-Control` de la funcion con `max-age=0, must-revalidate` --- MEDIDO en la URL viva, `X-Cache: MISS` --- y el CDN no cacheaba nada: la funcion habria corrido una vez POR USUARIO, que es justo el coste que todo este diseno evita. Con extension, la unica regla que casa es `**`, que no pone cache, y sobrevive el `Cache-Control` por RESPUESTA (120 s con ocupacion viva, 3600 s sin ella). La funcion esta en `europe-west1` como las otras dos, porque Firestore vive en `eur3` y la ocupacion del ticket 3 la va a leer de ahi. ⛔ Y su respuesta la cachea el CDN: sin eso la funcion correria una vez POR USUARIO en vez de una vez por celda y TTL.

POST autenticado, por instalación, nunca cacheado — no necesita la extensión `.json` que mergeCell sí necesita para esquivar el Cache-Control de las rutas sin extensión. [MKT-INSTALL-ATTRIBUTION-CHANNEL-001]

redirects.//: Marketing shortcuts (social bios, QR, campaigns) → the Play listing, each one carrying WHERE THE CLICK CAME FROM. The base URL is `PLAY_URL` from web/lib/config.mjs, duplicated here because firebase.json cannot import it; WebSiteParityGuardrailTest checks they agree. ⛔ The `referrer` parameter is the ONLY thing that survives the hop into the store: a UTM-tagged bio link loses its query there, and a 301 to a fixed URL drops the incoming one too — so without this, Play files every one of these installs as organic and GA4 as (direct), and nobody can tell whether the account brought one install or three hundred. ⛔ Its value is PERCENT-ENCODED (%3D, %26): a literal `&` inside it splits into separate Play parameters, the link still opens the store, and the attribution is lost with no error at all. ⛔ One entry per exact source, never an @(a|b|c) alternation — same lesson as the header rules below, which deployed clean and matched nothing. `utm_medium` separates earned (social) from bought (paid): without it the spend cannot be divided by anything. [MKT-AN-INSTALL-MUST-SAY-WHERE-IT-CAME-FROM-001]
Territory links: one per creative territory of docs/marketing/INSTAGRAM-GROWTH-STRATEGY.md §5.2, so the acquisition report says WHICH IDEA brought people and not just 'Instagram'.

Paid zone links: `utm_medium=paid`, one per bought radius (§9). The install is attributed per ZONE, not per ad — which ad works is what Meta's own CTR is for, and a route per ad would multiply paths and guardrails for nothing.

Second earned source: the account's OWN Facebook page link, same shape as the Instagram bio above but naming `facebook`. This is not the Facebook placement inside the paid Instagram campaign — that stays excluded (INSTAGRAM-GROWTH-STRATEGY.md §9.3). [MKT-ADD-FACEBOOK-ATTRIBUTION-ROUTE-001]

headers.//: Everything under /assets is content-hashed by web/build.mjs (site.<hash>.css), so a changed file is a different URL and a cached copy can never be the wrong one. That is what earns `immutable`. ⛔ The previous max-age=900 on unhashed css/js shipped a real bug: HTML revalidates immediately, css did not, so a returning visitor got new markup painted by the previous stylesheet for a quarter of an hour.
The manifest is the one file under /assets that is NOT hashed; it must never be pinned.

An icon entry point that CANNOT be hashed: the browser and the manifest spec ask for it by this exact path. Without a rule it matches none of the other sources and inherits Hosting's default max-age=3600, which hides a redeploy [WEB-THE-FAVICON-IS-THE-ONE-ASSET-THAT-CAN-GO-STALE-001]. The drawings these point AT are hashed; only the doorways revalidate. ⛔ One rule per path, never an @(a|b|c) alternation of full paths: that form deployed clean and matched NOTHING, and the only thing that showed it was reading Cache-Control off the live URL [WEB-A-HOSTING-HEADER-RULE-MUST-ACTUALLY-MATCH-001].

The pre-cooked car-park base [OSM-PRECOOKED-SNAPSHOT-001]. A published snapshot is IMMUTABLE under its week — a regeneration writes a NEW version and the pointer moves at the end — so the cells earn `immutable` for the same reason /assets does: a changed cell is a different URL and a cached copy can never be the wrong one. ⛔ The two rules are ordered exactly like /assets/** followed by /assets/manifest.json, which is the shape that is deployed and working: the specific one comes AFTER the general one. ⛔ And one glob per path, never an @(a|b|c) alternation of full paths — that form deployed clean and matched NOTHING [WEB-A-HOSTING-HEADER-RULE-MUST-ACTUALLY-MATCH-001], so this must be verified by reading Cache-Control off the live URL, not from this comment.

The POINTER, and the one file here that must never be pinned — same doorway rule as /favicon.ico. ⛔ A `.json` matches none of the other sources and would inherit Hosting's default max-age=3600, which hides a regeneration for an hour: readers would keep fusing last week's cells while the new ones sat published and unused.

With cleanUrls the browser asks for /terms, not /terms.html, and header rules match the REQUEST path — so the rule above never fires for a page and Hosting's default max-age=3600 applies, hiding a redeploy for an hour. These two cover the extensionless paths and the directory roots.
